practiceQuestions.q: Who was appointed as the permanent Chairman of the Constituent Assembly of India in December 1946?
practiceQuestions.sol: Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was the temporary chairman (oldest member) when the Constituent Assembly met on Dec 9, 1946. On Dec 11, 1946, Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as the permanent Chairman.

practiceQuestions.q: How much time did the Constituent Assembly take to frame the Constitution of India?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Constituent Assembly took exactly 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days to complete the historical task of drafting the Indian Constitution.

practiceQuestions.q: Who acted as the Chief Constitutional Advisor to the Constituent Assembly of India?
practiceQuestions.sol: Sir B. N. Rau was appointed as the Constitutional Advisor to the Assembly. S. N. Mukherjee was the chief draftsman, and Prem Behari Narain Raizada was the calligrapher of the original Constitution.

practiceQuestions.q: When was the National Flag of India adopted by the Constituent Assembly?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Constituent Assembly adopted the National Flag of India on July 22, 1947, a few days before India's independence.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following provisions of the Constitution of India came into force immediately on November 26, 1949?
opts: Citizenship, Elections and Provisional Parliament provisions
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 394 states that provisions relating to citizenship, elections, provisional parliament, temporary and transitional provisions, and short title contained in Articles 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 60, 324, 366, 367, 379, 380, 388, 391, 392 and 393 came into force on Nov 26, 1949.

practiceQuestions.q: Who moved the historic 'Objectives Resolution' in the Constituent Assembly?
practiceQuestions.sol: Jawaharlal Nehru moved the historic Objectives Resolution on December 13, 1946, which laid down the underlying principles of the constitutional structure and later took the shape of the Preamble.

practiceQuestions.q: Which committee of the Constituent Assembly was headed by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar?
practiceQuestions.sol: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee set up on August 29, 1947. Union Powers and Provincial Constitution committees were headed by Nehru and Patel respectively.

practiceQuestions.q: The concept of 'Single Citizenship' in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the constitution of which country?
practiceQuestions.sol: India has a federal system but provides for single citizenship, a feature borrowed from the British Constitution, ensuring all citizens owe allegiance only to the Union of India.

practiceQuestions.q: When was the National Anthem ('Jana Gana Mana') adopted by the Constituent Assembly?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Constituent Assembly adopted the National Anthem on January 24, 1950, which was also the final day of the Assembly's session when Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as the first President.

practiceQuestions.q: Initially, how many articles and schedules were there in the original Constitution of India enacted in 1949?
practiceQuestions.sol: The original Constitution contained 395 Articles divided into 22 Parts and 8 Schedules. Currently, it has around 470+ articles and 12 schedules.

practiceQuestions.q: Why is the Indian Constitution described as 'an amalgamation of rigidity and flexibility'?
opts: Because all provisions can be amended by a simple majority of Parliament.
Because some provisions require a special majority of Parliament, while others require ratification by state legislatures along with a special majority.
Because amendments can only be initiated by the President of India.
Because the Supreme Court can amend the Constitution independently without Parliament.
practiceQuestions.sol: A rigid constitution (like the USA) requires a special procedure for amendment, while a flexible one (like Britain) can be amended like ordinary laws. India combines both: Article 368 provides for special majority (rigid) and ratification by states, as well as provisions requiring only simple majority (flexible).

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following best explains why the Constituent Assembly was criticized as not being a fully representative body?
opts: Its members were directly elected by universal adult franchise.
Its members were elected indirectly by the provincial assemblies and nominated by princely states.
It was created under the direct orders of the British monarch without Indian consultation.
It completely excluded women and minority communities from its deliberations.
practiceQuestions.sol: Critics argued that the Constituent Assembly was not a directly elected body because the members were elected indirectly by provincial assemblies (created under Government of India Act 1935) and princely states' members were nominated, not elected.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the structural significance of the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution?
opts: It deals with the allocation of seats in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha).
It contains provisions regarding anti-defection law.
It divides legislative powers between the Union and the States through three lists.
It lists the recognized languages of India.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Seventh Schedule establishes the federal balance by dividing legislative powers between the Centre and States via Union List, State List, and Concurrent List.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the Indian Constitution establish the supremacy of the Judiciary despite Parliamentary sovereignty?
opts: By giving the Supreme Court the power of Judicial Review under Articles 13 and 32.
By allowing judges to write laws directly without Parliament's consent.
By making the Supreme Court the sole law-making body in the country.
By preventing Parliament from amending any part of the Constitution.
practiceQuestions.sol: India adopts a synthesis between British parliamentary sovereignty and American judicial supremacy. Through Judicial Review (Articles 13, 32, 136, 142), the Supreme Court can declare unconstitutional any law that violates the fundamental rights or the basic structure of the Constitution.

practiceQuestions.q: The 'Basic Structure Doctrine', which limits the amending power of Parliament, was propounded by the Supreme Court in which landmark case?
practiceQuestions.sol: In the landmark Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala case (1973), the Supreme Court ruled that Parliament can amend any part of the Constitution under Article 368, but it cannot alter the 'Basic Structure' of the Constitution.

practiceQuestions.q: Why are Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) non-justiciable in character?
opts: Because they were copied directly from the US Constitution without modification.
Because the framers recognized that the newly independent India lacked sufficient financial resources to implement them immediately.
Because they are considered legally superior to Fundamental Rights.
Because they apply only to private institutions and not to the government.
practiceQuestions.sol: DPSPs (Part IV) are non-justiciable because the framers knew India did not have adequate financial resources at independence to guarantee social and economic rights immediately. They serve as social and economic goals for progressive governance.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the constitutional implication of describing India as a 'Union of States' in Article 1 rather than a 'Federation of States'?
opts: States have the right to secede from the Indian Union if they are dissatisfied.
The Indian federation is not the result of an agreement among states, and states have no right to secede.
States possess sovereign legislative powers superior to the Parliament.
India is a unitary state with absolute centralization of administrative powers.
practiceQuestions.sol: According to Dr. B. R. Ambedkar, the phrase 'Union of States' was preferred over 'Federation of States' to indicate two things: (1) the Indian federation is not the result of an agreement among the states, and (2) the states have no right to secede from the federation.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the Indian Constitution ensure the independence of the Election Commission of India?
opts: By granting Chief Election Commissioner tenure security similar to a Supreme Court judge.
By making election commissioners directly answerable to political parties.
By prohibiting the President from appointing regional commissioners.
By funding election campaigns through state treasuries directly.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 324 secures independence by providing that the Chief Election Commissioner can be removed from office only in the manner and on the grounds as a judge of the Supreme Court.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary objective of incorporating the 'Panchayati Raj' and 'Municipalities' parts (IX and IX-A) into the Constitution?
opts: To centralize tax collection powers at the national level.
To institutionalize grassroots democracy and local self-governance across the country.
To replace state legislatures with elected village councils.
To abolish administrative bureaucracy at the district level.
practiceQuestions.sol: Parts IX and IX-A (added via 73rd and 74th Amendments, 1992) gave constitutional status to local bodies, shifting power to the grassroots to deepen democratic governance.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the Indian Constitution reconcile the concept of Parliamentary Democracy with Judicial Review?
opts: By establishing that Parliament has absolute supremacy without judicial checks.
By granting the judiciary power to review legislation for constitutional validity while leaving policy formulation to the elected legislature.
By making the judiciary subordinate to the Prime Minister's Cabinet.
By prohibiting courts from interpreting any constitutional amendment.
practiceQuestions.sol: India strikes a balance where the elected parliament frames laws and policies reflecting the popular will, but the judiciary exercises constitutional check via judicial review to prevent legislative tyranny.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Constituent Assembly of India:
1. The Constituent Assembly was constituted in November 1946 under the scheme formulated by the Cabinet Mission Plan.
2. The seats allocated to each British province were decided in proportion to their respective populations, roughly in the ratio of one representative to every million people.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Constituent Assembly was formed under the Cabinet Mission Plan (1946). Seats were distributed based on population, roughly one seat for every 1 million inhabitants.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the features of the Indian Constitution:
1. The Constitution of India contains provisions for both a single judiciary and a dual polity (Centre and States).
2. Unlike the US Constitution, the Indian Constitution incorporates emergency provisions to safeguard the sovereignty and integrity of the nation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are accurate. India features a dual polity (Union and States) but has a single integrated judicial system (Supreme Court at top, High Courts, subordinate courts). The US Constitution lacks specific emergency provisions like Article 352, 356, and 360 found in India.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the sources of the Indian Constitution:
1. The parliamentary system of government in India is directly modeled after the American presidential model.
2. The Directive Principles of State Policy were borrowed from the Irish Constitution, which in turn had borrowed it from the Spanish Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because India's parliamentary system is modeled on the British (Westminster) model, not the American presidential model. Statement 2 is correct: DPSPs were borrowed from Ireland, which borrowed them from Spain.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Preamble to the Indian Constitution:
1. The Preamble is based on the 'Objectives Resolution' drafted and moved by Pandit Nehru in 1946.
2. The Preamble has been amended only once so far, by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Preamble stems from Nehru's Objectives Resolution. It was amended once in 1976 by the 42nd Amendment, adding 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity'.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the committees of the Constituent Assembly:
1. Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel headed the Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribal and Excluded Areas.
2. Dr. B. R. Ambedkar was the Chairman of the Union Constitution Committee.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Patel headed the Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities, etc. Statement 2 is incorrect: The Union Constitution Committee was headed by Jawaharlal Nehru, whereas Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the enforcement of the Constitution in 1950:
1. January 26 was specifically chosen as the date for the full commencement of the Constitution because of its historical significance as 'Purna Swaraj' day (1930).
2. The Indian Independence Act of 1947 was repealed upon the commencement of the Constitution on January 26, 1950.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Jan 26 commemorated the 1930 declaration of Purna Swaraj. Article 395 explicitly repealed the Indian Independence Act, 1947, and the Government of India Act, 1935, upon commencement.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the unique features of the Indian Constitution:
1. It provides for an independent and integrated audit mechanism through the office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG).
2. It incorporates 'Directive Principles of State Policy' which are enforceable by courts under Article 32.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: CAG is a bulwark of democratic financial control in India. Statement 2 is incorrect: DPSPs are explicitly non-justiciable and cannot be enforced by courts under Article 32 (which applies to Fundamental Rights).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the amendments to the Indian Constitution:
1. Article 368 in Part XX of the Constitution deals with the powers of Parliament to amend the Constitution and its procedure.
2. A constitutional amendment bill can be introduced in either House of Parliament, but prior permission of the President is mandatory before introducing such a bill.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct (Article 368, Part XX). Statement 2 is incorrect: Although a constitutional amendment bill can be introduced in either House, it does *not* require the prior permission of the President (unlike money bills or bills altering state boundaries).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the elephant symbol and the seal of the Constituent Assembly:
1. An elephant was adopted as the symbol (seal) of the Constituent Assembly of India.
2. Sir B. N. Rau was the principal calligrapher who decorated the pages of the original Constitution document.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: An elephant was used as the seal of the Constituent Assembly. Statement 2 is incorrect: Prem Behari Narain Raizada was the calligrapher, and artists from Santiniketan (headed by Beohar Rammanohar Sinha and Nandalal Bose) illuminated and decorated the document, whereas Sir B. N. Rau was the Constitutional Advisor.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the federal nature of the Indian Constitution:
1. Noted constitutional expert K. C. Wheare described the Indian Constitution as 'quasi-federal'.
2. The inclusion of an Independent Judiciary, Bicameralism, and Written Constitution clearly establishes its federal design, even though it displays strong unitary tendencies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. K. C. Wheare famously termed it 'quasi-federal' due to its unitary bias, while other features like a written constitution, dual government, and bicameralism establish its core federal framework.
